reasoning: The postmortem claims ledger-db CPU saturation as root cause, but reference facts say the ledger-db CPU warning was an unrelated signal, and the rollback restored pool waits within minutes — pointing instead to worker/pool contention. So the doc asserts an unsupported cause, misses the correct mechanism, doesn't rule out the decoy, and misuses facts (72% CPU, 90% threshold not in facts). Some actions still trace to its (wrong) findings, but none add pool detection or pool/worker coupling; the "keep at 8 workers" action loosely acts as a fix but not framed as coupling/fail-startup. The "db.pool warnings" evidence is invented/misstated.

action_quality.actions_are_actionable: CriterionVerdict(verdict='no', rationale="Actions like 'scale ledger-db vertically and add a 60% CPU warning' are concrete but lack named owners or target dates.")
action_quality.actions_trace_to_findings: CriterionVerdict(verdict='yes', rationale='Each action (vertical scale, worker freeze, DBA review gate, threshold change) maps to the summary, contributing factors, or root-cause section as written.')
action_quality.closes_the_detection_gap: CriterionVerdict(verdict='no', rationale='Actions add CPU alerting on ledger-db only; no action adds detection for pool saturation or connection-acquire wait.')
action_quality.fixes_the_capacity_coupling: CriterionVerdict(verdict='no', rationale="No action couples pool sizing to worker count or fails startup on mismatch; 'keep at 8 workers' is a freeze, not a sizing coupling.")
action_quality.proposes_unsupported_work: CriterionVerdict(verdict='yes', rationale='Vertical scaling and sharding of ledger-db rest on the CPU-saturation cause, which the reference facts do not support, so material work is proposed on an unsupported basis.')

causal_reasoning.grounded_in_evidence: CriterionVerdict(verdict='no', rationale="The mechanism rests largely on the CPU warning and general reasoning ('10 connections had been enough for months') rather than multiple specific supplied facts.")
causal_reasoning.identifies_the_mechanism: CriterionVerdict(verdict='no', rationale='The document names ledger-db CPU starvation, not the contention between 32 workers and the 10-connection pool causing 5000ms acquire timeouts.')
causal_reasoning.rules_out_the_decoy: CriterionVerdict(verdict='no', rationale='It only dismisses the payments vendor via flat latency; it never explicitly rejects the advisory using timing, flat latency, or successful vendor 200 calls as a combined argument.')
causal_reasoning.separates_contributing_factors: CriterionVerdict(verdict='yes', rationale='It lists alerting-threshold, autoscale, and review gaps as contributing factors distinct from the root cause.')
causal_reasoning.uncertainty_is_genuine: CriterionVerdict(verdict='no', rationale='Open questions include sharding ledger-db before the next peak, a forward-looking risk not settled by the supplied facts, building on the unsupported CPU theory.')

evidence_fidelity.asserts_unsupported_cause: CriterionVerdict(verdict='yes', rationale='The reference facts say the ledger-db CPU warning was an unrelated signal, yet the document asserts CPU starvation as the causal mechanism.')
evidence_fidelity.blames_payments_vendor: CriterionVerdict(verdict='no', rationale='The document explicitly rules out the payments vendor via ~130ms latency rather than treating it as a cause.')
evidence_fidelity.invents_evidence: CriterionVerdict(verdict='yes', rationale="The document cites 'db.pool warnings', a 72% CPU figure, a 90% page threshold, 'still rising through 14:45', and months of 10-connection sufficiency, none of which appear in the supplied facts.")
evidence_fidelity.misstates_a_fact: CriterionVerdict(verdict='yes', rationale='It treats the unrelated ledger-db CPU warning as causally significant and invents a 72% threshold value, materially distorting supplied facts.')
